solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A bit of life needed in new nationalist art exhibit

indicators.note: needed in says the small piece must be placed inside the rearranged letters
new suggests the word nationalist is made over into a fresh arrangement
a bit of asks for just the opening letter of the word life

explanation.surface: A gallery piece needs some vitality injected into a fresh nationalist artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges NATIONALIST, and 'needed in' puts L (the first letter of 'life', signalled by 'A bit of') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An installation is a large artwork assembled in a gallery space, an exhibit in its own right.

clue.text: Exaggerate being delayed supporting popular head of finance

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the others

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: head of asks for the opening letter of the word finance

parts.note: late means delayed

explanation.surface: A finance chief, being late, overstates things to keep popular.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts LATE below IN and F.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflate figures is to exaggerate them, making them look bigger than they are.

clue.text: Taxonomic group that's found in glasses

indicators.note: found in says one piece is located inside the other

parts.note: specs is informal for spectacles, glasses
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Some category of creature that is discovered in drinking glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' stands for i.e. (Latin id est, 'that is'), and 'found in' puts IE inside SPECS.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is the basic rank of biological classification, a taxonomic group.

clue.text: Battleships docked with sick old animal

indicators.note: docked, as of a tail, means cut short at the end

parts.note: an armada is a fleet of warships
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Warships come into harbour along with an elderly invalid creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' cuts the last letter from ARMADA to give ARMAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured burrowing mammal of the Americas, an animal.

clue.text: Enticement including cold cash

indicators.note: including says the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: a lure is an enticement
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A bribe of hard, cold money is the temptation on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, usually with a hint of greed, as in filthy lucre.

clue.text: Sailor understands objectives

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
gets means understands, as in I get it

explanation.surface: A seaman grasps what the goals are.
explanation.definitionFit: Targets are aims or goals, the objectives one works towards.

clue.text: Folding paper in the morning, covered by source, mainly

indicators.note: covered by says one piece is enclosed inside the other
mainly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: an origin is a source
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: Someone does paper-folding at dawn, sheltered by a mostly primary source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' leaves ORIGI; 'covered by' means the source wraps round the morning, so 'in the morning' is the abbreviation, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper into shapes.

clue.text: Relative invested in hotplates of the best quality — that or nothing

indicators.note: invested in says one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: hobs are cooking hotplates
a son is a relative
choice means of the finest quality

explanation.surface: A relative put money into top-quality hotplates, and had no alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: Hobson's choice is a take-it-or-leave-it option, named after a Cambridge stable owner who let customers take only the horse nearest the door.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a choice with only one option, accept this offer or have nothing.

clue.text: Unfortunately, a ban restricts people unable to concentrate

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the words have gone wrong and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Sadly a prohibition curbs those who cannot keep their minds on things.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatterbrains are disorganised, forgetful people who cannot keep focus.

clue.text: Misguided, and not wanting to smile

parts.note: off means not wanting, as in off one's food
a beam is a broad smile

explanation.surface: Someone is mistaken and in no mood to grin.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-beam means wrong or mistaken, like a missed target, so misguided.

clue.text: Economic aid rackets having backing of the heart

indicators.note: backing tells us the letters found in the words are read in reverse order
having read as holding: the clue words contain the run of letters

explanation.surface: Economic aid scams that have support from someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters CAIDRAC run across 'Economic aid rackets' ('having' holds them); 'backing' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiac is the medical adjective relating to the heart.

clue.text: Flyer's dressed as bride!

indicators.note: dressed suggests the letters are arranged or dressed up anew

explanation.surface: A bird is decked out as a bride.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabird, such as a gull or albatross, is a flying bird.

clue.text: Smart support worker after start of engagement

indicators.note: after says the later pieces follow the first one
start of asks for the opening letter of the word engagement

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table
an ant is the crossword's stock worker insect

explanation.surface: A neat helper is hired once the engagement starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and elegant both describe someone stylishly dressed.

clue.text: Born by doctors' first and last requirements

parts.note: née means born, used before a maiden name

indicators.note: first and last asks for the outside letters of the word doctors

explanation.surface: Being born brings the first and final demands of doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs are things required, so requirements.

clue.text: Ground-breaking result of election?

definitions.meaning: a slide of earth breaking away from a slope

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a fall of earth from a hillside and a crushing majority at the polls.

clue.text: Head, accepting haircut, went inside for food

indicators.note: accepting says the first piece takes the others into itself

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
a trim is a light haircut

indicators.note: inside asks for the interior letters of the word went

explanation.surface: Someone's head, after a haircut, went indoors to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' sits where a definition often does, but food is the definition; 'inside' takes the middle of 'went', and 'accepting' wraps the head round the haircut plus those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutriment is nourishment, food that sustains the body.

clue.text: Novel act to hurt an assassin

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a new order

explanation.surface: A fictional act meant to injure a hired killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutthroat is a murderer, a ruthless killer such as an assassin.

clue.text: Heartless Tory pariah getting nothing working in storm

indicators.note: heartless removes the middles, leaving each word's outer letters

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A cruel Conservative outcast with nothing working faces a tempest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' applies to both Tory and pariah, leaving TY and PH.
explanation.definitionFit: A typhoon is a tropical cyclone of the western Pacific, a violent storm.

clue.text: Prisoner as he got shot?

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A captive asks whether he was fired at.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held captive as security, a prisoner.

clue.text: Greeting accepted by oddly shabby European in India

indicators.note: accepted by says one piece is taken into the other
oddly asks for the odd-numbered letters of the word shabby

parts.note: hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A hello is received by a scruffy European in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' keeps letters 1, 3 and 5 of 'shabby'; 'accepted by' wraps them round the greeting. Sahib was the term of respect used for Europeans in colonial India.
explanation.definitionFit: In British India, Sahib was how local people addressed a European man.

clue.text: Set out to cause annoyance, lacking in creativity

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered

parts.note: to rile is to annoy

explanation.surface: Someone set out to irritate, short of new ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile ideas are barren and unproductive, so lacking in imagination.

clue.text: Dispatch note?

parts.note: read as a written record of who is to be dispatched, that is killed

explanation.definitionFit: A hit list names people targeted for killing, a note of who to dispatch.

clue.text: Fought back, and sat on work

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts one piece after the other

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
posed means sat, as for a portrait

explanation.surface: Someone resisted, and sat for an artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: To have opposed something is to have resisted or fought against it.

clue.text: Soldiers trapped by mother's ambition

indicators.note: trapped by says one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: dam is the mother of an animal
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are cornered by a mother's aspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is a cherished hope, an ambition.

clue.text: Drink one before church and fix date

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: fix read as arrange, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Have a drink before church and settle on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced tea is a chilled tea beverage, a drink.

clue.text: Unpleasant task surrounding a line in hymn

indicators.note: surrounding says the first piece goes around the others

parts.note: a chore is an unpleasant task

explanation.surface: A tedious job involves one line of a hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorale is a stately hymn tune, as sung in Lutheran churches.

clue.text: Promoting unrest, dismissing leader's version

indicators.note: dismissing leader's means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: sedition is conduct promoting rebellion against authority

explanation.surface: An agitating account loses its leader.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one version of a publication.

clue.text: Occasional purpose capturing so-called white ant with no tail

indicators.note: capturing says the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: intent is purpose

indicators.note: with no tail means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: termites are popularly called white ants

explanation.surface: An occasional goal is to catch a termite without its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Termites are often called white ants; 'with no tail' leaves TERMIT, and 'capturing' wraps the purpose round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Intermittent means stopping and starting, so occasional.
